title: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy: Algorithms and Performance Analysis
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
layout_note: Server cloud top left; a row of N client devices across the bottom, each with its own model glyph and database below; an adversary icon at the far left intercepts the uploads.
grouping: No containers; each client is a device photo-icon (phone, laptop, desktop) labelled C_1..C_N, with a node-link network glyph to its left and a grey database cylinder (Database i) below; an ellipsis stands for the rest. A boxed legend top right explains the two arrow styles.
shapes_depth: Clip-art: light-blue cloud for the server, device photos, grey 3-D cylinders, a red devil for the adversary. Arrows: solid dark-blue for uploads labelled w_i, dashed dark-blue for broadcasts labelled w, a thick blue block arrow carrying w_1 ... w_N to the adversary; inside each client short green arrows (model training loop) and orange arrows (data access). Bold math labels.
proposed_highlight: The threat, not the method, is emphasised: the adversary is the only red element and receives a heavy arrow carrying every client's uploaded parameters.
lesson: Separate upload and broadcast by line style (solid w_i up, dashed w down) and key it in a small boxed legend; mark the eavesdropper as the only red icon fed by a heavy arrow of all uploads.
notes: Venue from Semantic Scholar (IEEE TIFS); year = arXiv preprint year.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: federated learning with differential privacy threat model
taxonomy.note: training 'other' = differential-privacy noise added to client uploads

core.what: one server cloud at top exchanges parameters with N parallel clients along the bottom, each client a device-model-database unit, via paired up (w_i) and down (w) arrows

relations.form: clients C1, C2 ... CN repeated left to right along the bottom, each the same unit of a device icon, a node-link model glyph to its left and a database cylinder below, with an ellipsis for the omitted clients
each client is tied to the server by a solid upward arrow labelled w_i and a dashed downward arrow labelled w running side by side
the single server cloud at top-left broadcasts the same w to every client and to the adversary
within each client green arrows loop from the database up to the model and from model to device and back, an implied local training cycle
the red devil Adversary at far left receives a dashed w from the server and a fat blue arrow carrying w1 ... wN, drawn beside the first client

channels.colour: blue = parameter transmission (both up and down), green = local model-data exchange, orange = device to database link, red = the adversary; the fat blue arrow reuses transmission blue for eavesdropped uploads
channels.shape: clip-art icons: cloud = server, phone/laptop/desktop = clients, node-link glyph = local model, cylinder = local data, devil = adversary
channels.line: solid blue = uploading, dashed blue = broadcasting, as keyed in the top-right legend
channels.frame: only the legend is framed; client units are grouped by proximity, not frames

quality.strengths: The upload/broadcast distinction is carried by one channel (solid vs dashed) with a legend, and the repeated client unit along the bottom makes the N-client federation readable at a glance; the adversary's interception is placed right beside the uplink it taps.
quality.weaknesses: Long parallel diagonal arrow pairs to C2 and CN fan out from the cloud and crowd each other; clip-art devices take most of the area while the method's contribution, the added noise for differential privacy, is not drawn anywhere; the fat blue adversary arrow reuses the transmission colour.

insights.structure: A cloud labelled Server at top-left, a row of clients along the bottom (phone C1, laptop C2, desktop CN with an ellipsis), each with a small network glyph and a database cylinder beneath, and a red devil Adversary at the far left.
insights.data: Clients are realistic device icons, local models small blue node-link networks, and local data grey cylinders labelled Database 1..N; parameters are written as w and w_i on the arrows.
insights.emphasis: The adversary is a red devil icon with a fat blue arrow carrying w1...wN into it, making the eavesdropping threat the eye-catching element.
insights.flow: Solid blue arrows go up from clients to the server (uploading w_i) and dashed blue arrows come back down (broadcasting w); green arrows loop between database and model, orange arrows link device and database.
insights.avoid: Clip-art device and cloud icons dominate and the long diagonal arrows pairs to far clients are crowded; the privacy mechanism itself (noise) is not drawn.

arrangement.units: unboxed icons: a cloud server, device clients with model glyphs and database cylinders
arrangement.inputs_as: database cylinder icons under each client
arrangement.shared: one server broadcasting the same w to all clients
